issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method has a signature with two parameters (String, boolean) while the problem statement's UML and the solution implement a single-parameter findStockIngredient(String). In the template, other Stock methods (add, take) already call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, which creates a compilation error and prevents students from following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.findStockIngredient method match the UML and solution by providing a single-parameter signature public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Alternatively, add an overloaded single-parameter method that delegates to the two-parameter version. This resolves compilation errors and aligns template, problem specification, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method that takes a single String parameter, but the template's Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive) (two parameters). This mismatch creates confusion for students: the UML and solution refer to a single-argument API while the starter code exposes a different signature, making it unclear which method to use or implement and causing potential compilation or mapping issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem UML and the solution by providing a single-argument method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either change the existing two-parameter signature to the single-argument form or add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing method (e.g., calling findStockIngredient(name, false)). This keeps the starter code aligned with the exercise description and the reference solution.
